$comment: SINGLE SOURCE for the task status vocabulary — the white ladder. Every surface (Elixir paper emitters, the paper-surface CSS tone tokens, and eventually Go pdrender + web) derives its glyphs, roles, and semantic colours from THIS file. Do not hand-edit a glyph or tone in any surface; edit it here and let the generators + drift gate carry it. scripts/status-manifest-check.sh regenerates the CSS tone block and gates every surface against this manifest.

platform_overrides.$comment: A RECORDED, ADJUDICATED divergence — never a silent exemption. A surface listed here renders the named role differently from the roles table above, because conforming would be WRONG on that platform, and scripts/status-manifest-check.sh reads this map as the expected value rather than hardcoding an exception. The gate also holds each entry HONEST: the role must exist in `roles`, the override must actually differ from the manifest glyph, and the set of diverging roles on that surface must equal the set listed here — so a second divergence can never hide behind the first, and an override that stops earning its keep reds instead of rotting. Adding a row here is a RULING and must carry its reason.

progress.reason: The manifest gives `progress` an EMPTY glyph with spinner:true because the web paints an empty span whose ::before CSS-animates the Braille frames. A React Native block renderer is pure by mobile charter D50 (no hooks), so there is no animation to run and an empty glyph would paint a blank cell in the board lane. Mobile therefore ships the half-filled circle it already uses for in_progress in its chat todo vocabulary, keeping the app internally consistent rather than importing the web's reduced-motion fallback frame. Mobile CONFORMING here would be a regression, which is why the ruling lives in the manifest and not as a skip in the checker. Adjudicated under mob-bl-status-manifest-mobile-gate.
